newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo may get $100 million Czech credit soon-papers.
newsitem.headline: Yugo may get $100 million Czech credit soon-papers.

text.p: The Czech Republic is close to granting a $100 million credit to Yugoslavia, the Czech ambassador in Belgrade was quoted by the daily Politika as saying on Wednesday.

"The Czech Republic is ready to grant a $100 million credit to Yugoslavia. Negotiations have been under way for 18 months and I hope they will be concluded soon," Ambassador Ivan Busniak was quoted by Politka as saying.
The loan would be used to finance the purchase of equipment for the Yugoslav power plant Kolubara B.
Busniak heads a Czech economic delegation including representatives of 13 of the country's top firms on a three-day visit to Yugoslavia.

There is interest on both sides to renew bilateral economic cooperation, especially in seven leading spheres -- electronics, machine-building, chemical industry, non-ferrous and ferrous metallurgy, construction and automobile industry, Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce official Bosko Markovic said.
Yugoslavia and the Czech republic signed an accord on trade cooperation in September 1996.

Busniak said the two countries were yet to sign accords on avoiding double taxation and mutual protection of investments, which he said would round off the legal frameworks for comprehensive economic cooperation.
The two sides agreed Yugoslav-Czech trade could reach half a billion dollars within a few years. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
